info.title: AnsibleForms API v2
info.description: API documentation for AnsibleForms v2 endpoints: Authentication, Query, Expression, AWX, Job, Backup, Credential, and Known Hosts management.

get.description: Returns the current version of the AnsibleForms application. No authentication required.
Returns help content from help.yaml configuration file.

schema.description: Help data parsed from YAML file

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's profile information.

put.description: Updates the password for the authenticated user. Only works for local users (not LDAP/Azure/OIDC).

400.description: Bad request - missing password or LDAP user

get.description: Returns all groups or find a specific group by name (query parameter).

400.description: Group has users or unknown group

get.description: Returns application settings (mail server, URL, etc.). Mail password is masked.

put.description: Updates the settings row. Config CONTENT is deliberately not accepted here : it is written through PUT /settings/config, which validates it, honours the designer lock and the baseHash concurrency check, and writes a restore point.

mail_password.description: Use '**********' to preserve existing password, empty string to clear, or new password

config_source.description: Where the active config is read from and written to

get.description: Returns the active config.yaml content, read from the source set in config_source (database, use_for_config repository or local file). The returned baseHash is a sha256 fingerprint of that content; send it back on PUT to detect a concurrent change.

forms_yaml.description: The active config.yaml content (empty string when there is none yet)

baseHash.description: sha256 fingerprint of forms_yaml, for optimistic concurrency on save

put.description: Validates the supplied yaml against the base schema and writes it to the active config source (database, use_for_config repository or local file). Refused while the designer holds the config lock.

forms_yaml.description: The full config.yaml content (categories, roles, constants)

baseHash.description: Optional baseHash from GET /settings/config; when sent, the save is refused with 409 if the active config changed in the meantime

400.description: Missing forms_yaml, invalid yaml, or config that fails the base schema validation

409.description: The active config changed elsewhere (stale baseHash)

423.description: Configuration is locked by the designer

put.description: Loads the config.yaml (or the deprecated forms.yaml) file into the database, replacing the database copy. A restore point of that database copy is written to the backups first. Refused while the designer holds the config lock.

423.description: Configuration is locked by the designer

put.description: Writes the database config out to the config.yaml file (the repository copy when a use_for_config repository holds it). A restore point of the old file is written to the backups first. Refused when the database is not the active config source or holds no config, and while the designer holds the config lock.

400.description: The database is not the active config source, or there is no config in the database to export

423.description: Configuration is locked by the designer

get.description: Returns whether the active form configuration lives in the database, resolved from the config_source setting with the ENABLE_CONFIG_IN_DATABASE environment default as fallback. Designer access is enough, so a designer without settings access can learn the mode.

configInDatabase.description: True when the active config is stored in the database

500.description: Failed to get the forms config

get.description: Returns a sorted, de-duplicated flat list of the form names, for the form dropdown of schedules. Subforms are excluded because they cannot be launched standalone.

500.description: Failed to get the forms list

post.description: Sends a test email to verify mail configuration.

to.description: Email address to send test to

post.description: Executes a SQL query against one or more configured database credentials. Supports multiple database types (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, Oracle, MongoDB) and optional jq filtering.

oneOf.description: Array of credential names to query (results merged)
Credential object with name and optional type

config.description: Database credential configuration (name, array of names, or object)

jq.description: Optional jq expression to filter/transform results

post.summary: Evaluate a form field's server expression
post.description: Evaluates the expression of a form field. Send formName and fieldName (plus subformName for a field in a subform): the expression text is taken from the form definition, loaded with the caller's roles, and only the placeholder values come from the request. A raw `expression` is accepted only from a user with settings or designer access.

formName.description: The root form holding the field

subformName.description: The subform holding the field, when it is not on the root form

fieldName.description: The field whose expression is evaluated

values.description: What each placeholder resolved to, keyed by the text between $( and )

literals.description: The keys of values that are spliced in as JSON (objects, arrays, records)

expression.description: A raw JavaScript expression - settings or designer access only

schema.description: Expression result (type varies: string, number, boolean, array, object)

403.description: A raw expression without settings or designer access, or a form the caller may not use

404.description: The form, subform or field does not exist or has no server expression

post.description: Use basic authentication to obtain a JWT token. Then use the access token, prefixed with 'Bearer', to use all other APIs. The access token is limited in time. You can login again to get a new set of tokens or use the /token API and the refresh token to obtain a new set (preferred).

expiryDays.description: Expiry days, requires extendedTokenExpiration option to be set to true in role-options

post.description: Use the refresh token to obtain a new access token.

get.description: Provider (anthropic, openai, azure, gemini, grok, mistral, deepseek, groq, openrouter, ollama, custom), model, base URL, auth type, api version, user, extra headers and limits. The api key comes back masked. Needs showSettings.

put.summary: Update the chat assistant's model provider
put.description: The api key is stored encrypted ; send it masked (**********) to keep the stored one. Refused (403) while the row is managed by the config seed.

auth_type.description: How the key is sent ; empty for the provider's default

request_user.description: Sent as user (OpenAI) or metadata.user_id (Anthropic), e.g. for a proxy ; empty sends none

extra_headers.description: A JSON object of extra request headers

ignore_certs.description: Skip the certificate check of the provider (a self-signed proxy). Insecure.

400.description: Invalid settings, e.g. extra headers that are not a JSON object

403.description: Managed by the config seed, or no showSettings

post.summary: Test the chat model provider with one tiny call

502.description: The provider could not be reached or refused

post.summary: Relaunch job by ID, as it ran or with some fields changed
post.description: Without a body the job is replayed with the extravars it ran with. With a body holding `values`, the values the job was launched with are taken, `values` is laid over them, and the result goes through the form engine again - resolved, validated and the extravars built by the server - as a new launch by the caller. Uploads of the original are reused. Without a body, or for a form under launch validation 'enforce', see the Launch validation page : a relaunch that goes through the check is refused (400) for a password field the form shows, since passwords are never stored with the field values ; one its dependencies hide does not count. Only for the job's owner, an admin or a user who sees every job. Needs the form to allow relaunch and the allowJobRelaunch role option.

parameters.name: verbose
parameters.description: Verbose ansible output (needs the allowVerboseMode role option)

values.description: Only the fields to change, as raw field values, keyed by field name

200.description: Job relaunched ; the new job id

400.description: A wizard form, a password field the form shows (relaunch through the check), or stored form data of another form

403.description: Relaunch or verbose mode not allowed

404.description: Job or form not found, or no stored form data (relaunch with values)

422.description: The changed values break the form's rules ; details list the failing fields and rows

get.summary: The raw field values a job was launched with, for a relaunch
get.description: Field name to raw value, as the form held them. Constants and passwords (also inside list rows) are never stored. Needs the form to allow relaunch and the allowJobRelaunch role option.

400.description: The stored data is corrupted or belongs to another form

404.description: Job or form not found, or the job has no stored form data

get.description: Runs every health check in parallel - database, schema, disk, jobs, scheduler, backups, designer lock, repositories, config seed, Vault, expression sanitizer, LDAP, storage and writable folders - and lists facts about this instance. Side-effect free. Requires settings access.

info.description: Facts with no pass/fail verdict (version, node, timezone, ...)

500.description: Failed to run the health check

get.description: Newest first. Every filter is optional and exact, except target, which matches a substring. Requires settings access.

500.description: Failed to read the audit trail

get.summary: Distinct actions and actors in the audit trail
get.description: For filter dropdowns. Requires settings access.

500.description: Failed to read the audit trail

post.description: Re-applies the file in CONFIG_SEED_PATH immediately, even when it has not changed (the same as SIGHUP). See https://ansibleforms.com/seed. Requires settings access.

summary.description: created, updated, adopted and unchanged items per section

400.description: No config seed configured (CONFIG_SEED_PATH is not set)

500.description: The seed could not be applied - the configuration in force is kept

post.summary: Restore the managed environment file from a backup
post.description: Puts the persistent/.env saved in the backup back in place. It takes effect after a restart.

200.description: Result - restored is false with a reason when the backup holds no environment file

get.description: Every variable documented in help.yaml, with its current value and whether it can be edited from the settings page. Secret values are masked. Requires settings access.

set.description: True when set in the environment

value.description: Current value, or the default when not set; masked for secrets

overridden.description: Set in the real environment, so it cannot be changed here

500.description: Failed to read the environment variables

put.description: Writes the given variables to the managed persistent/.env. An empty value or null clears the variable back to its default. Variables marked live take effect immediately; the others are listed in restartRequired. Refused when ALLOW_ENV_EDIT=0, for variables that cannot be edited from the UI, and for variables set in the real environment. Requires settings access.

400.description: Unknown, refused or invalid variable, or nothing given

403.description: Environment editing is disabled (ALLOW_ENV_EDIT=0), or no settings access

409.description: The variable is set in the real environment and cannot be changed here

post.description: Read-only: looks up the token, nothing is written. Requires settings access.

ttl.description: Seconds left, null when the token does not expire

400.description: Vault is not configured, unreachable or refused the token

get.summary: List the KV mounts in Vault
get.description: Only kv mounts. Requires settings access.

400.description: Vault is not configured or unreachable

get.summary: Is the active config a ytt template
get.description: True when the active config.yaml contains ytt annotations (#@), in which case the designer must not save its rendered output over it. Designer access is enough.

500.description: Failed to read the forms config

get.summary: Public application settings for the UI
get.description: Navigation label and icon, and the server-wide default language and theme. Not wrapped in the usual result envelope. No authentication required.
Reports whether the AnsibleForms schema and tables are present and complete. No authentication required.

500.description: The schema is missing or incomplete

post.description: DROPS AND RECREATES EVERY TABLE. Allowed without authentication only on a database that is not provisioned yet (fresh install); on a provisioned database it needs an authenticated administrator. Refused entirely when ALLOW_SCHEMA_CREATION=0. An empty database also creates its schema by itself at startup.

401.description: The database is already provisioned and the request is not authenticated

500.description: Failed to check or create the schema

bearerAuth.description: JWT Bearer token. Authenticate via /auth/login, then use 'Authorize' here.

Runner.description: Where a job runs. type rte : a runtime environment container (AF_ROLE=rte) for playbooks. type awx : AWX / Ansible Automation Platform / Ascender for templates.

token.description: rte : its RTE_TOKEN. awx : an API token (or use_credentials)

use_credentials.description: awx : sign in with username and password instead of a token

is_default.description: Used by playbook forms that name no runner

flavour.description: awx : which product it is, Ansible Automation Platform or Ascender ; none is AWX. Its uri may carry its API path (https://aap.example.com/api/controller/v2)

node_id.description: rte : the RTE that registered this runner itself (RTE_REGISTER) ; empty when added by hand or by the config seed

state.description: Only on a runner an RTE registered itself : automatic while that RTE writes its heartbeat, unresponsive once it stopped (removed by the worker after 10 minutes)

SecretStore.description: A secret store. Which fields are used depends on the type.

cache_ttl_seconds.description: 0 reads the secret on every use

extra.description: JSON object with options of the store type

user.description: Database user (leave empty when using a secret store).

password.description: Database password (leave empty when using a secret store).

credential_type.description: What the credential is for ; is_database follows it

secret_store.description: Name of the secret store user and password are read from.

secret_ref.description: Where the secret lives in the store, e.g. a Vault path.

vault_path.description: Deprecated since 7, removed in 8 : the same as secret_store 'vault' with this secret_ref.

formName.description: Name of the form to launch.

job_type.description: Type of job (e.g., ansible, awx, multistep).

OAuth2Provider.description: OAuth2 provider configuration object (Azure AD, OIDC, etc.).

id.description: Unique identifier for the OAuth2 provider.

tenant_id.description: Azure AD tenant ID (for Azure AD providers).

client_secret.description: OAuth2 client secret. Use '**********' to preserve existing secret when updating.

enable.description: Enable this provider (1 = enabled, 0 = disabled). Only one provider of each type can be enabled.

userinfo_url.description: User info URL (optional, auto-discovered for OIDC).
